name: Partial Equivalence Queries Complexity / Self-Directed Queries Complexity
details: For finite concept classes, $\mathrm{LC}_{\mathrm{partial}}(\mathcal H)\ge\mathrm{SDC}(\mathcal H)$.
proof: Corollary 8(1) of Doliwa--Fan--Simon--Zilles states the chain $\mathrm{RTD}(\mathcal H)\leq\mathrm{SDC}(\mathcal H)\leq\mathrm{LC}_{\mathrm{partial}}(\mathcal H)$.  Its middle inequality is the simulation established by Goldman--Sloan: the partial-equivalence-query model is no more powerful than self-directed learning, so its optimal worst-case query count cannot be smaller.
witness_verification: Fix any $d\ge1$ and let $n$ grow.  Then $\mathrm{SDC}(\mathrm{BOX}_n^d)=2$ while $\mathrm{LC}_{\mathrm{partial}}(\mathrm{BOX}_n^d)=\Theta(d\log n)$, so the gap is unbounded and rules out every reverse affine-linear bound.
